title: Seven in the morning, cups still on

tokens.v: Full-bleed photograph, edge to edge, no border, frame or letterbox band. Seven in the morning in a narrow kitchen: he stands half-turned away with the canvas cups on, unaware of the lens, the straight side part holding its line. A materials frame: the near cup owns a third of the frame width, a pale disc against the shadowed wall behind. 85mm at f/2.8 a metre away, level with his ear; low window light from the left grazes across the oatmeal-beige cotton canvas so its over-under basket weave resolves warp thread by weft thread, the fine top-stitched seam round the cup readable, the cork headband lining granular, the matte ecru yoke arm flat and sheenless. The cup facing the lens is his left, entirely plain — no buttons, port or status light. The kettle's steam is the only thing between lens and product, climbing through the near-right across the cup's right edge and softening that edge alone. No hands and nothing below the chest in frame; an ecru waffle henley collar is the only wardrobe. Wall cabinets cut the top edge, the counter runs out the bottom, the doorway blurs at the left.
